bio: Leslie A. Guerra is a vocalist, recording artist, and music industry professional with more than twenty-five years of experience spanning live performance, recording, artist development, label operations, A&R, marketing, and entertainment management.
name: Leslie Ann Guerra
bioES:
Sus créditos artísticos incluyen giras como vocalista de apoyo junto a los íconos del reggaetón Don Omar (2006–2015) y J Álvarez (2015–2020), presentándose ante audiencias en Estados Unidos, América Latina y Europa. También aparece en el lanzamiento en vivo King of Kings: En Directo, grabado durante la gira mundial King of Kings World Tour de Don Omar y publicado por Machete Music.

Guerra inició su carrera discográfica como integrante de Las Nenas del Swing, participando en producciones y grabaciones como Rompe Corazones, Chicle Bomba, Desearía y Me Faltas Tú. A lo largo de su trayectoria en giras y espectáculos, también participó en producciones que incluyeron artistas como Wisin & Yandel, Arcángel, Daddy Yankee, Natti Natasha y Melina León.

Más allá de los escenarios, Guerra ha ocupado posiciones de liderazgo, coordinación y operaciones dentro de la industria del entretenimiento. Se desempeñó como Coordinadora de A&R en Sony Music Latin, brindando apoyo a operaciones ejecutivas de A&R e iniciativas de desarrollo artístico. También coordinó operaciones artísticas y de manejo para Orfanato Music Group y Arrow Management, gestionó logística artística para Adam Torres Concerts y lideró iniciativas de mercadeo y relaciones públicas a través de NV Marketing & Public Relations.

Actualmente, Guerra combina su experiencia en interpretación, desarrollo artístico, operaciones, mercadeo y estrategia empresarial a través de proyectos creativos y empresariales, incluyendo PorfolioID, una plataforma profesional diseñada para ayudar a artistas, creadores y profesionales a presentar su trayectoria, logros y portafolio de manera moderna y organizada.

works.aboutWork: Vals Demente explores the emotional cycle of a relationship built on ego, manipulation, and repeated patterns. Rather than placing blame on one person, the song recognizes that both people continued dancing the same destructive dance until self-love finally became the way out.
works.aboutWorkEs: Vals Demente explora el ciclo emocional de una relación construida sobre el ego, la manipulación y los patrones repetidos. En lugar de culpar a una sola persona, la canción reconoce que ambas personas continuaron bailando el mismo baile destructivo hasta que el amor propio finalmente se convirtió en la salida.
works.description: A haunting dance between love, temptation, and the emotional cycles we struggle to escape.
works.inspiration: A real relationship that repeated the same cycle of distance and return until self-love became the way out.
works.creativeNotes: Recorded originally: iPhone Voice Memo. The title and chorus image — "un seis cilindros con el motor caliente" — came from picturing the relationship as a car running hot, going nowhere, just cycling in place.

behindTheLyrics.story:
That lyric came from a real experience.

At the time, I knew almost nothing about cars beyond driving them.

About a month after paying off my Dodge Charger—my favorite car—my daughter was involved in an accident that totaled it.

When I replaced it, I bought a newer Dodge Charger without realizing much about its performance features.

One winter day, while the car was stuck in the snow, I accidentally switched it into Sport mode.

The car couldn't move because it was trapped in the ice, but the engine suddenly roared to life.

I had no idea what I had done.

The sound was intense.

My first thought was that if the car hadn't been stuck, I might have driven straight into my former employer's house.

That moment stayed with me.

Years later, while writing Vals Demente, I remembered that engine—powerful, loud, unpredictable, and ready to launch before I was.

It became the perfect metaphor for the emotional intensity of the relationship.

That's where the lyric came from.

Sometimes the most unexpected moments become the lines people remember most.

works.storyBehindWork:
I began writing "Vals Demente" on February 26, 2020.

The original lyrics and hook were captured that day in an iPhone voice memo, preserving the song's earliest form exactly as it first came to me.

At the time, I was trying to make sense of a relationship that felt like an endless cycle—love, distance, hope, disappointment, and beginning again.

The hook came almost immediately.

“Un vals demente, un seis cilindros con un motor caliente...”

That single phrase captured everything I was feeling at the time.

The song itself, however, took much longer to reveal its final melody and form.

Although the first draft captured exactly how I felt in that moment, I wasn't ready to finish it.

Something remained unresolved because, in many ways, I was still living the story I was trying to write.

So the song waited.

Years passed.

Life continued.

I experienced new beginnings, painful endings, personal growth, and long periods of reflection.

Without realizing it, I was changing—and as I changed, so did the meaning of the song.

When I returned to "Vals Demente" on June 17, 2026, I wasn't the same woman who had started writing it.

I no longer heard it as a story about someone else's choices.

I heard it as a story about my own.

I realized the cycle wasn't only created by another person.

It continued because I kept returning to it, hoping that this time things would be different.

The song became less about heartbreak and more about awareness.

Finishing it wasn't simply a creative milestone.

It was a personal one.

For the first time, I could see the dance for what it was—and choose to step out of it.

That's why "Vals Demente" isn't simply a breakup song.

It's a song about recognizing a pattern.

It's about reclaiming your voice.

It's about choosing yourself.

And ultimately...

it's about breaking the cycle.

works.aboutWork: Yahweh, Yo Te Pertenezco is a song about returning. Written after a season of quiet distance from God, it traces the journey from emptiness back to belonging — the courage it took to sit down outside a closed door, and the peace that followed once she realized she had never truly been left waiting. It is worship as testimony: not a song about becoming religious, but about coming home.
works.aboutWorkEs: Yahweh, Yo Te Pertenezco es la historia de un regreso — no uno triunfal, sino uno silencioso. Escrita después de una etapa en la que me sentí lejos de Dios, la canción refleja lo que significa volver a casa: dejar de huir, sentarse, orar, y descubrir que la puerta nunca estuvo realmente cerrada. Es una canción de pertenencia, escrita por alguien que alguna vez dudó si merecía pertenecer.
works.description: A deeply personal prayer of surrender, belonging completely to God through every season of life.
works.inspiration: The realization that belonging was never lost, only forgotten — and that everything in creation already belongs to the One who made it, the singer included.
works.creativeNotes: Born from a season of quiet return rather than dramatic revelation — the song carries peace more than performance. Inspired by the image of a single open chair outside a closed church door, an invitation that never withdrew. Built in a South African Afro-house and gospel-leaning direction, with spiritual chanting, call-and-response choir, rhythmic claps, and a melodic hook in the spirit of “Jerusalema” — joy expressed as movement, not just declaration.
works.descriptionEs: Una canción de adoración sobre pertenecer completamente a Dios.

behindTheLyrics.story: This is the line the whole song turns on. “Yo te pertenezco” doesn't mean losing who she is — it means finally discovering where her identity belonged all along. The line that follows makes the shape of it clear: “Como el río al mar, mi alma te obedece” — like the river to the sea. A river doesn't disappear when it reaches the ocean. It arrives at what it was always moving toward.

works.storyBehindWork:
There was a time in my life when I knew about God, but I didn't truly know Him.

That season is hard to describe. It wasn't simple loneliness. It was a quiet emptiness — the feeling that something essential was missing, even while life went on around me.

I often wondered why I felt disconnected.

Why I never quite felt whole.

More than anything, I carried the weight of feeling undeserving.

Everything began to change in February 2024.

God has a way of reaching us through the people and moments we least expect. One unexpected lesson led me to the doorstep of a church one evening.

The church was closed.

But outside sat a single chair.

The curtains were open, almost as if the invitation remained even after the doors had been locked.

So I sat down. I prayed.

That night, I found my way back to God.

It took courage to return — not because I doubted Him, but because I wasn't sure I deserved to come back.

Then I realized something beautiful.

He had never left. He had been waiting for me all along.

From that night forward, my life began to change — not all at once, but deeply, quietly, and permanently.

Peace slowly replaced fear. Purpose replaced confusion. Hope replaced emptiness. Healing replaced shame.

On November 13, 2025, at 10:00 AM, I wrote the first composition of “Yahweh, Yo Te Pertenezco.”

The title means “Yahweh, I Belong to You.” Those words carry everything I could never fully say in conversation.

This song is my thank you. It is my worship. It is my testimony.

God gave me the gift of music long before I understood why He had given it to me. Writing this song felt like returning that gift to its rightful place.

Every time I sing it, I remember the woman I used to be, and I thank God for the woman He has helped me become.

The song kept growing as my relationship with God deepened.

On May 6, 2026, at 8:44 PM, I re-recorded and completed it in its final form.

If Vals Demente tells the story of a heart trapped in unhealthy patterns, Yahweh, Yo Te Pertenezco tells the story of what happened after healing.

It is the sound of coming home.

My prayer is simple. That anyone who hears this song will know that no one is ever too far gone, too broken, or too undeserving to return to God.

If He was waiting for me, I believe He is waiting for you too.

El 15 de septiembre de 1998, Luis Fonsi hizo su debut oficial en Guaynabo, Puerto Rico, con el lanzamiento de su primer álbum de estudio, *Comenzaré*. Durante ese mismo evento, el grupo *Las Nenas del Swing* presentó por primera vez su sencillo *Chicle Bomba*, tema incluido en su producción discográfica debut, *Rompe Corazones*.

Fue allí donde tuve la dicha de conocer a quien, con el paso de los años, se convertiría en una de las figuras más importantes e influyentes de la música latina: Luis Fonsi. Lo que comenzó como el encuentro entre dos artistas que daban sus primeros pasos en la industria musical se transformó en el inicio de una trayectoria extraordinaria que lo llevaría a alcanzar reconocimiento internacional y a consolidarse como un ícono de la música en español.

Don Omar se presentó con un rotundo éxito en el Festival Internacional de la Canción de Viña del Mar el martes 23 de febrero de 2010. Esta mítica actuación marcó su segunda aparición en la Quinta Vergara (tras su debut en 2007) y consolidó su posición como el "Rey de Reyes" del reguetón ante el exigente público chileno. El show estuvo fuertemente marcado por la estética futurista de su álbum iDon, lanzado el año anterior.

Este concierto fue transmitido completamente en vivo por televisión abierta y señal internacional. El Festival de Viña del Mar es uno de los eventos televisivos más importantes de la música latina, por lo que toda la presentación de Don Omar el 23 de febrero de 2010 llegó a millones de hogares.

En Chile: La transmisión oficial en televisión abierta estuvo a cargo de una histórica alianza entre los canales chilenos Canal 13 y Televisión Nacional de Chile (TVN). Hito tecnológico: Esa edición de 2010 fue histórica para la televisión chilena, ya que fue la primera vez que el festival se transmitió completamente en Alta Definición (HD) a través de la señal de Canal 13. A nivel internacional: El show se emitió hacia toda Latinoamérica y Estados Unidos mediante señales de cable asociadas y cadenas como A&E y TV Chile (la señal internacional de TVN).

King of Kings: Live is a live album by Puerto Rican reggaeton singer Don Omar, released in 2007, through Machete Music. Recorded on December 2006, at the José Miguel Agrelot Coliseum in San Juan, Puerto Rico, it captures a high-energy concert performance featuring 19 tracks across two CDs, blending upbeat reggaeton anthems with emotive R&B-style ballads. 

Spanning a total runtime of approximately 73 minutes, the setlist includes fan favorites like "Conteo," "Bandoleros," and "Dile," alongside slower, introspective numbers such as "Vuelve," "Angelito," and "Pobre Diabla," which highlight Don Omar's vocal range and ability to incorporate strings and traditional instruments into reggaeton's typically rhythmic framework. 

It was nominated for Urban Album of the Year at the 2009 Lo Nuestro Awards. Despite these, it underscored Don Omar's creative prowess and contributed to his reputation as reggaeton's most dynamic performer at the time, with the live renditions amplifying the genre's party atmosphere while revealing subtler balladry. The album was also released in DVD format, allowing fans to experience the full concert visuals, further cementing its role in Don Omar's discography as a pivotal live document of his 2006-2007 peak.

I had the privilege of working alongside AJ "El Kallejero" Ramos during my Don Omar era at Arrow Management. Long before becoming one of the most influential executives in Latin music and culture, AJ was already demonstrating the vision, work ethic, and leadership that would define his career.

Over the years, I witnessed firsthand his resilience, dedication, and unwavering commitment to the growth of Latin music. Beyond being an exceptional professional, AJ became a trusted colleague and friend.

I will always be grateful for the support and encouragement he provided while I worked at Don Omar, as well as throughout my time working with Natti Natasha and Momo. His guidance, generosity, and belief in the people around him helped shape the careers of many, including my own.

Today, AJ serves as Head of Artist Partnerships for Latin Music and Culture at YouTube, where he continues to champion Latin artists and help drive the global growth of our culture. It has been inspiring to watch his journey and well-deserved success.

Thank you, Mofongo, for your friendship, support, and the countless memories we shared along the way. I am forever grateful. May God continue to bless you, your family, and everything you do. Proud of you!

Don Omar, Sinfónico" en el Coliseo de Puerto Rico José Miguel Agrelot es considerado uno de los experimentos más vanguardistas y arriesgados en la historia de la música urbana. Celebrado el viernes 18 de abril de 2008, el espectáculo rompió los esquemas tradicionales del reguetón al fusionar el ritmo callejero con la música clásica. 

La orquesta en vivo: El autodenominado "Rey" del reguetón estuvo respaldado por más de 40 músicos profesionales de la Orquesta Sinfónica de Puerto Rico y estudiantes destacados del Conservatorio de Música. El director musical y responsable de adaptar las partituras fue el reconocido maestro Ángelo Torres.

El repertorio sinfónico: Ante más de 6,000 personas, las canciones abrieron con arreglos de cuerdas imponentes. El espectáculo inició con "Dale Don dale", seguido de éxitos adaptados magistralmente como "Ronca", "Repórtense", "Pobre Diabla" y "Salió El Sol".

Contexto personal: El concierto tuvo una carga emocional única, ya que se produjo en una única función y sirvió como antesala formal a su mediática boda con la presentadora de televisión Jackie Guerrido, la cual se celebró exactamente al día siguiente, el sábado 19 de abril de 2008.

bioFull:
Her performance credits include touring as a supporting vocalist for reggaeton icons Don Omar (2006–2015) and J Álvarez (2015–2020), appearing before audiences throughout the United States, Latin America, and Europe. She is featured on the live release King of Kings: En Directo, recorded during Don Omar’s King of Kings World Tour and released by Machete Music.

Guerra began her recording career as a member of Las Nenas del Swing, contributing to recordings including Rompe Corazones, Chicle Bomba, Desearía, and Me Faltas Tú. Throughout her touring career, she also performed on productions featuring artists such as Wisin & Yandel, Arcángel, Daddy Yankee, Natti Natasha, and Melina León.

Beyond the stage, Guerra has held leadership and operational roles throughout the entertainment industry. She served as A&R Coordinator at Sony Music Latin, supporting executive A&R operations and artist development initiatives. She also coordinated artist and management operations for Orfanato Music Group and Arrow Management, managed artist logistics for Adam Torres Concerts, and led marketing and public relations initiatives through NV Marketing & Public Relations.

Today, Guerra combines her experience in performance, artist development, operations, marketing, and business strategy through creative and entrepreneurial ventures, including PorfolioID, a professional platform designed to help artists, creators, and professionals showcase their work, accomplishments, and career journeys.

credits.fullDesc: Las Nenas del Swing — Recording Artist / Founding Member Before Las Nenas del Swing was formed, Leslie A. Guerra was already establishing herself as a performer throughout Puerto Rico, appearing at venues including Hotel Intercontinental and Hotel San Juan. It was during a Sunday performance at Rancho de los Trovadores in Cayey that Elvis Crespo and Wilfredo Ortiz walked in — and everything changed. That night led to an audition with producer Luis Corporán and her selection as a founding member of Las Nenas del Swing. On September 10, 1998, Las Nenas del Swing released Rompe Corazones, an 11-track tropical and merengue album released through R&R Music, distributed in Puerto Rico by Combo Records and in the United States through Rimas Records in New York. Managed by Ramón Rivera, who also managed Grupo Karis, the group developed a growing fan base throughout Puerto Rico, the Caribbean, and major East Coast Latino markets. As a founding member and featured vocalist, Leslie contributed to several of the album’s best-known recordings, including Chicle Bomba, Desearía, and Me Faltas Tú. The project featured contributions from respected musicians and vocalists within the tropical music genre, including backing vocal participation by Elvis Crespo, Juan Castro (Tony Tun Tun), and Juan Luis Guzmán. Production credits included Freddy Méndez on piano and Luis Corporán on saxophone. During the promotional cycle for Rompe Corazones, Las Nenas del Swing shared stages with prominent tropical and merengue acts including Los Hermanos Rosario, El Gran Combo de Puerto Rico, Grupo Karis, Grupo Manía, Grupo Mambo, Manny Manuel, Tony Tun Tun, Melina León, and Gisselle. The group also participated in performances associated with the New York Puerto Rican Day Parade and appeared throughout Puerto Rico, Connecticut, Pennsylvania, Massachusetts, and the Dominican Republic. Rompe Corazones represents Leslie Guerra’s earliest documented commercial recording credit and the beginning of a professional music career that would later expand into international touring, artist development, label operations, marketing, A&R, and entertainment management. Today, the album remains available through major digital streaming platforms, preserving an important chapter in Puerto Rican tropical music and serving as the foundation of Leslie’s decades-long career in the music industry. Special thanks to Melissa, Marie, and Kadmara — and to Elvis Crespo, Wilfredo Ortiz, Ramón Rivera, Juan Luis Guzman, Luis Corporán, Freddie Méndez, and Raúl Armando Del Valle for their guidance, support, and belief during the formative years of this journey.

Fue durante una actuación dominical en el Rancho de los Trovadores en Cayey que Elvis Crespo y Wilfredo Ortiz entraron al lugar — y todo cambió. Esa noche llevó a una audición con el productor Luis Corporán y a su selección como miembro fundadora de Las Nenas del Swing. El 10 de septiembre de 1998, Las Nenas del Swing lanzaron Rompe Corazones, un álbum de 11 pistas de tropical y merengue bajo R&R Music, distribuido en Puerto Rico por Combo Records y en Estados Unidos por Rimas Records en Nueva York. Bajo la gestión de Ramón Rivera, quien también representaba a Grupo Karis, el grupo desarrolló una creciente base de seguidores en Puerto Rico, el Caribe y los principales mercados latinos de la Costa Este. Como miembro fundadora y vocalista destacada, Leslie contribuyó a algunas de las grabaciones más reconocidas del álbum, incluyendo Chicle Bomba, Desearía y Me Faltas Tú. El proyecto contó con la participación de reconocidos músicos y vocalistas del género tropical, incluyendo coros de Elvis Crespo, Juan Castro (Tony Tun Tun) y Juan Luis Guzmán. Los créditos de producción incluyen a Freddy Méndez en piano y Luis Corporán en saxofón. Durante el ciclo promocional de Rompe Corazones, Las Nenas del Swing compartieron escenarios con destacadas figuras del tropical y el merengue, incluyendo a Los Hermanos Rosario, El Gran Combo de Puerto Rico, Grupo Karis, Grupo Manía, Grupo Mambo, Manny Manuel, Tony Tun Tun, Melina León y Gisselle. El grupo también participó en presentaciones asociadas al Desfile Puertorriqueño de Nueva York y se presentó en Puerto Rico, Connecticut, Pensilvania, Massachusetts y la República Dominicana. Rompe Corazones representa el primer crédito comercial de grabación documentado de Leslie Guerra y el inicio de una carrera musical profesional que se expandiría hacia giras internacionales, desarrollo artístico, operaciones discográficas, mercadeo, A&R y gestión del entretenimiento. Hoy, el álbum sigue disponible en las principales plataformas digitales de streaming, preservando un capítulo importante de la música tropical puertorriqueña y sirviendo como la base de la carrera de Leslie en la industria musical. Un agradecimiento especial a mis compañeras Melissa, Marie y Kadmara — y a Elvis Crespo, Wilfredo Ortiz, Ramón Rivera, Juan Luis Guzman, Luis Corporán, Freddie Méndez y Raúl Armando Del Valle por su guía, apoyo y confianza durante los años formativos de este camino.

Nine Years with Don Omar From 2006 through 2015, Guerra served as Don Omar's exclusive touring female vocalist during one of the most influential periods in Latin urban music — including collaborative performances where Don Omar shared the stage with artists such as Daddy Yankee, Arcángel, and Wisin & Yandel. Her work from this era is permanently documented on King of Kings: En Directo, released internationally by Machete Music on CD and DVD and broadcast nationally through DirecTV in 2007. Following her tenure with Don Omar, Guerra became the exclusive touring vocalist for J Álvarez, the renowned Puerto Rican reggaetón and Latin urban recording artist, from 2015 through 2020. Together, these roles established a live performance career spanning nearly two decades and positioned Guerra among the few women to maintain long-term featured vocal roles across multiple internationally touring reggaetón productions. Building the Business Behind the Music While performing internationally, Guerra simultaneously built an extensive career in business operations and executive support. From 2001 to 2006, she served as a Human Services Specialist with the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), helping determine eligibility for federal disaster assistance following major national emergencies, including the September 11 attacks and Hurricane Katrina. As her career evolved, Guerra expanded into executive operations, compliance, artist management, A&R coordination, marketing, and artist relations across the entertainment industry, including a leadership role at Arrow Management and A&R coordination at Sony Music Latin. The combination of live performance experience and executive operations became Guerra's defining professional advantage. Having worked both on stage and behind the scenes, she developed a unique understanding of the creative, technical, and business challenges facing entertainment professionals through leadership in artist relations, operational systems, compliance, and customer relationship management (CRM). Founder, porfolioID Drawing upon both halves of her career — performance and operations — Guerra founded porfolioID, a professional identity platform she conceived, designed, and built from concept to deployment. She defined the platform's architecture, feature set, and bilingual user experience, drawing directly on her own career as the platform's first real-world use case: a professional record built on verified credits, documented history, and proof — not assumption. Guerra continues to invest in her professional and technical education, including a Bachelor of Applied Science (BAS) in Supervision and Management at Polk State College and CS50's Introduction to Artificial Intelligence with Python through Harvard University's School of Engineering and Applied Sciences. She previously completed a Computer Support Technician Diploma at Florida Technical College (NUC University), graduating with High Honors and a 4.0 GPA. Today, Guerra continues to bridge entertainment, business, and technology through porfolioID, bringing together decades of experience to help professionals preserve, verify, and showcase the careers they have worked to build.
